nfs_protocol_version.title: NFS Protocol Version
nfs_protocol_version.description: The NFS protocol version in use for this mount or export. NFSv2 and NFSv3 transmit all data in cleartext with no transport security options. NFSv4+ with appropriate security flavor or TLS can provide encryption, integrity, and authentication.

nfs_security_flavor.title: NFS Security Flavor (sec= option)
nfs_security_flavor.description: The security flavor negotiated or configured for NFS mounts and exports. 'sys' uses weak UID/GID-based AUTH_SYS with no encryption or mutual authentication. 'auth_none' provides no authentication. Kerberos flavors (krb5, krb5i, krb5p) provide progressive authentication, integrity, and privacy. Only krb5p encrypts the data payload. 'tls' provides transport encryption on NFSv4.2+.

nfs_tls_enabled.title: NFS over TLS Enabled (xprtsec/RFC 9289)
nfs_tls_enabled.description: Whether NFS traffic is encrypted using TLS at the transport layer (xprtsec=tls or xprtsec=mtls per RFC 9289, available in NFSv4.1+ with kernel TLS support). True indicates transport encryption is enforced, providing both confidentiality and integrity for all NFS traffic including Kerberos ticket exchange.

rpcsec_gss_enabled.title: RPCSEC_GSS (Kerberos) Authentication Enabled
rpcsec_gss_enabled.description: Whether RPCSEC_GSS with Kerberos is configured for this NFS mount or export (sec=krb5, krb5i, or krb5p). Provides sequence-number-based replay protection and mutual authentication. krb5i adds per-message integrity; krb5p adds full encryption.

rpcsec_gss_integrity_enabled.title: RPCSEC_GSS Integrity Protection Enabled (krb5i/krb5p)
rpcsec_gss_integrity_enabled.description: Whether RPCSEC_GSS with integrity protection (sec=krb5i or sec=krb5p) is configured, providing per-message MICs to detect in-transit tampering. krb5i provides integrity without encryption; krb5p provides both integrity and privacy.

kerberos_configured.title: Kerberos (RPCSEC_GSS) Infrastructure Configured
kerberos_configured.description: Whether Kerberos-based mutual authentication (RPCSEC_GSS) is fully operationally configured for this NFS deployment, including keytab presence with nfs/ principal, rpc.gssd/gssproxy service running, and KDC reachability. All three conditions must be true.

auth_flavor.title: NFS Authentication Flavor
auth_flavor.description: The RPC authentication flavor negotiated for the NFS mount (AUTH_SYS/AUTH_UNIX, AUTH_NONE, RPCSEC_GSS/Kerberos variants). AUTH_SYS relies on client-asserted UID/GID with no cryptographic verification. AUTH_NONE provides no authentication.

kerberos_encryption_types.title: Kerberos Encryption Types Permitted
kerberos_encryption_types.description: List of Kerberos encryption types negotiated or permitted in the KDC/client configuration. Weak types such as rc4-hmac, des-cbc-md5, or des3-cbc-sha1 increase susceptibility to offline cracking of intercepted tickets.

rpcbind_network_exposure.title: rpcbind/portmapper Network Exposure
rpcbind_network_exposure.description: Whether rpcbind/portmapper (port 111 TCP/UDP) is accessible from untrusted or external network segments, enabling interception and spoofing of port assignments that redirect NFS clients to attacker-controlled services.

portmapper_response_authentication_enabl.title: Portmapper Response Authentication Enabled
portmapper_response_authentication_enabl.description: Whether cryptographic authentication or integrity verification of rpcbind/portmapper responses is enforced (via RPCSEC_GSS at the portmapper level or static port configuration bypassing portmapper lookup). Default rpcbind offers no response authentication.

nfs_traverses_routed_segments.title: NFS Traffic Traverses Routed Network Segments
nfs_traverses_routed_segments.description: Whether NFS traffic crosses one or more routed network boundaries (passes through routers, crosses VLANs via L3, or traverses WAN links) rather than remaining on a single flat L2 segment. Increases exposure to routing manipulation attacks.

icmp_redirects_disabled.title: ICMP Redirects Disabled on NFS Hosts
icmp_redirects_disabled.description: Whether ICMP redirect message acceptance is disabled on both NFS client and server hosts, preventing route poisoning via ICMP redirect attacks that could redirect NFS traffic through an attacker-controlled host.

nfs_client_bandwidth_limit_configured.title: NFS Client Bandwidth Limit Configured
nfs_client_bandwidth_limit_configured.description: Whether per-client bandwidth or rate limiting controls are configured at the NFS server or network level (via export options, QoS policies, traffic shaping, or NFS server-side throttling) to prevent a single client from saturating the link.

nfs_network_qos_policy_applied.title: NFS Network QoS Policy Applied
nfs_network_qos_policy_applied.description: Whether a network-level QoS or traffic shaping policy is applied to the NFS transport path (on switch, router, or SDN fabric) that enforces bandwidth limits or prevents a single client from monopolizing the NFS network link.
